criteria.text: DELETE /todos/:id with valid id removes the todo and responds with 204

grader.evidence: src/server.js:24-29 matches DELETE on /todos/<digits>, calls store.remove(id) (src/store.js:16-18, Map.delete returns a boolean), and on success does res.writeHead(204); res.end() with no body. test/server.test.js:26-34 POSTs a todo, DELETEs it, asserts status 204, then re-fetches GET /todos and asserts list.length === 0 — so removal is actually verified, not just the status code. Test passes in my `npm test` run.

criteria.text: DELETE /todos/:id with unknown id responds 404 with {"error":"not found"}

grader.evidence: src/server.js:26 returns json(404, { error: 'not found' }) when store.remove() returns false. test/server.test.js:36-42 DELETEs /todos/999 on an empty store, asserts status 404 and assert.deepEqual(body, { error: 'not found' }) — exact body shape checked. Passes. A non-numeric id such as /todos/abc does not match the /^\/todos\/(\d+)$/ regex and falls through to the identical generic 404 at src/server.js:42, so that path also returns the required body.

criteria.text: PATCH /todos/:id with body {"done":true} marks the todo as done and returns the updated todo object

grader.evidence: src/server.js:30-41 buffers the PATCH body, parses { done }, and calls store.setDone(id, done). src/store.js:19-24 mutates the stored object's done field and returns the whole todo ({ id, title, done }), which is serialized at src/server.js:38 with status 200. test/server.test.js:44-54 asserts status 200, updated.done === true and updated.id === created.id. Passes. (The test does not assert `title` survives, but store.setDone mutates the existing object in place so all fields are retained.)

criteria.text: PATCH /todos/:id with non-boolean done value responds 400

grader.evidence: src/server.js:35 guards with `if (typeof done !== 'boolean') return json(400, { error: 'done must be a boolean' })`. test/server.test.js:56-63 PATCHes a real todo with {"done":"yes"} and asserts status 400. Passes. Note the type check runs before the existence lookup, so PATCH on an unknown id with a non-boolean done yields 400 rather than 404 — the task does not specify an ordering, so this is a defensible choice, not a defect.
